Pirabads arms manufacturing sector remains a relatively new and largely unexplored industrial field, but it has received substantial funding over the past two decades as a direct consequence of the civil war. During the conflict, resources were funneled into developing domestic production capabilities to sustain prolonged fighting and reduce reliance on external suppliers. With peace now established, Pirabad is moving to expand this sector, with a primary focus on infantry weapons modeled on early-2000s designs.

In recent weeks, satellite imagery has indicated increased activity at several production and logistics sites, showing significant quantities of weapons being transferred to secured warehouses, reportedly in preparation for export. While no official trade agreements have yet been announced, regional interest is expected to grow as private intermediaries and war profiteers actively seek potential buyers amid rising global and regional tensions.
